title: fix: honor Claude MCP config directory
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16288

- Read Claude's user-scope MCP file from `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, falling back to the home directory when unset or empty.
- Use that shared path for status, ownership/collision checks and stored-key recovery, so reinstall and removal find the entries created by native Claude.
- Extend the existing client tests with distinct home/config directories, default/empty controls, key recovery and a real Claude lifecycle preserving foreign entries.

Validation: two custom-directory regressions fail on baseline; all 284 CLI tests pass after the fix, including both native Claude lifecycle cases. Build, scoped Biome and diff checks pass. Strict TypeScript retains the same 35 existing diagnostics, byte-identical to baseline. Local checks used Node 24 and compatible cached dependencies; native Claude integration is conditional when the binary is absent. Configuration-only tests used temporary directories and synthetic keys.

gist.headline: Claude's config has an address
gist.blurb: Polli follows Claude to its chosen config directory. MCP installs, status checks, and removals can all find the same door.
gist.summary: The Polli CLI reads Claude's user-scope MCP file from CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, falling back to the home directory when it is unset or empty, and uses that path for status checks, collision checks, stored-key recovery, reinstall, and removal.
gist.impact: People using a custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR get consistent MCP management across installs and removals, while entries created by native Claude remain intact.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Claude's MCP configuration as a cozy directory-shaped garden shed with two paths: a marked custom-config path and a home-directory fallback. Polli, wearing a tiny explorer's hat, follows the custom path to tend her own code-plant while leaving another plant, representing native Claude's entries, undisturbed.
